subject: community-medicine
title: Food Adulteration: Argemone Oil, Sanguinarine and FSSAI Standards

steps.title: Argemone oil adulteration in edible oils
steps.tx: The predatory or negligent contamination of edible mustard oil with oil expressed from seeds of Argemone mexicana represents a catastrophic form of **food adulteration poisoning**. The toxic alkaloid sanguinarine, alongside dihydrosanguinarine, remains completely soluble and heat-stable in vegetable oil, resisting normal kitchen boiling and frying temperatures and producing devastating multi-system toxicity across entire households sharing a common cooking pot.
steps.say: Adulterating mustard oil with prickly poppy seeds introduces heat-stable sanguinarine poison. Boiling and deep-frying cannot destroy the toxin, which strikes everyone eating from the family pot.

left.title: Adulteration characteristics
points: Added fraudulently to increase profit margins
Yellow colour and viscosity mimic mustard oil
Toxin stable at high domestic frying heats

right.title: Clinical presentation in families
points: Bilateral pitting leg dropsy and breathlessness

steps.title: Nitric acid and paper chromatography detection tests
steps.tx: Food safety inspectors detect argemone contamination using rapid chemical screening methods, primarily the **nitric acid test for argemone**. Adding five millilitres of concentrated nitric acid to an equal volume of suspect oil in a test tube yields a characteristic brownish-red to orange-red ring at the liquid interface within minutes; laboratory confirmation uses thin-layer chromatography, where sanguinarine fluoresces bright golden-yellow under ultraviolet illumination.
steps.say: Food inspectors add concentrated nitric acid to test suspected mustard oil, producing a brown-red ring. Under ultraviolet laboratory light, sanguinarine glows bright golden-yellow.

nodes.label: Equal parts suspect oil and concentrated nitric acid
Shake gently and observe interface for 10 minutes

steps.title: Sanguinarine mechanism: capillary leakage and glaucoma
steps.tx: At the molecular level, **sanguinarine vascular toxicity** inhibits vascular endothelial sodium-potassium ATPase, depleting cellular energy and triggering profound capillary hyperpermeability. Massive extravasation of proteinaceous plasma fluid into subcutaneous tissues produces bilateral dependent dropsy, while fluid accumulation in uveal vascular tissue and trabecular meshwork causes acute intraocular pressure elevation, bilateral open-angle glaucoma, and optic nerve atrophy.
steps.say: Sanguinarine paralyzes the pumps that keep blood vessel walls tight. Massive fluid leaks out into the legs, while fluid trapped inside the eyes causes acute glaucoma and blindness.

rows: Bilateral pitting pedal oedema and erythema
Trabecular meshwork block and uveal oedema
Bilateral open-angle glaucoma with visual loss
Myocardial interstitial oedema and low resistance
High-output congestive cardiac failure and dyspnoea

steps.title: Endemic ascites: Crotalaria and pyrrolizidine alkaloids
steps.tx: Another lethal food-borne intoxication in central India is **endemic ascites outbreaks**, historically reported in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan when millet crops (little millet or Panicum miliare) are contaminated with weed seeds of Crotalaria species (jhunjhunia). Crotalaria seeds contain hepatotoxic pyrrolizidine alkaloids, specifically monocrotaline, which induce hepatic veno-occlusive disease, obliterating central hepatic venules and causing massive, painful ascites with high fatality.
steps.say: Endemic ascites occurs when weed seeds of Crotalaria contaminate harvested millet. The alkaloid monocrotaline blocks liver veins, triggering rapid, painful fluid buildup in the abdomen.

nodes.label: Millet crops contaminated with Crotalaria weed seeds
Subendothelial swelling of central hepatic venules
Hepatic veno-occlusive disease and massive ascites

steps.title: Common food adulterants and rapid home detection
steps.tx: Unscrupulous commercial vendors add harmful substances to common foodstuffs, creating pervasive **food adulterant hazards** across municipal markets. Common examples include adding lead chromate or metanil yellow dye to turmeric powder, brick powder to chilli powder, starch to milk, and mineral oil to edible oils; basic consumer awareness and household testing with dilute iodine or hydrochloric acid readily unmask these fraudulent practices.
steps.say: Traders cheat consumers by mixing starch into milk, chalk into flour, and toxic dyes into turmeric. Adding simple iodine turns starch purple, exposing watered-down adulterated milk instantly.

rows: Metanil yellow chemical dye, lead chromate
Carcinogenic dye; turns pink with conc. HCl
Brick powder, artificial red coal tar dyes
Stomach irritation; settles rapidly in water glass
Iodine turns blue for starch; lactometer checks water
Papaya seeds float in alcohol; repulsive bitter taste

steps.title: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
steps.tx: Established under the Food Safety and Standards Act of 2006, the **FSSAI regulatory authority** serves as the apex statutory body regulating the manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import of food products across India. Consolidating eight older conflicting food laws (including the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act of 1954), FSSAI sets science-based standards, licenses food business operators, deploys food safety officers, and conducts market surveillance.
steps.say: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India sets national food standards and licenses businesses. It consolidated older food laws to enforce strict hygiene from farm to dining table.

rows: Single unified national food safety code
Mandatory registration for all food business operators
Random inspection and chemical laboratory sampling
Prosecution and heavy fines for adulteration
Food Safety on Wheels mobile testing vans
Rapid doorstep detection of common adulterants

steps.title: National food fortification policy: the +F logo
steps.tx: To eradicate widespread micronutrient malnutrition without requiring individual pill compliance, FSSAI established comprehensive **food fortification standards**, introducing the standardized plus-F logo to identify verified fortified foods. Regulations establish precise fortification standards for five key staple food vehicles: wheat flour (atta) and rice fortified with iron, folic acid and B12; edible oils and milk fortified with vitamins A and D; and double fortified salt.
steps.say: The plus-F logo on food packets marks staple items enriched with vitamins and minerals. Fortifying ration rice, milk and cooking oil provides daily micronutrients without taking pills.

rows: Vitamin A and Vitamin D (retinyl palmitate)
Prevents night blindness and adult osteomalacia
Supports bone growth and mucosal child immunity
Dual protection against cretinism and anaemia

steps.title: Eat Right India movement and public campaigns
steps.tx: Complementing regulatory enforcement, FSSAI spearheads the multi-sectoral **Eat Right India movement**, built upon three interconnected pillars: Eat Safe, Eat Healthy, and Eat Sustainably. The campaign promotes front-of-pack traffic light labeling, certifies schools and campuses as Eat Right campuses, restricts the marketing of high-fat, high-sugar and high-salt (HFSS) ultra-processed foods to children, and trains street food vendors in hygienic food handling.
steps.say: The Eat Right India campaign urges families to cut salt, sugar and trans fats. It certifies clean school cafeterias and trains street food vendors to handle snacks safely.

nodes.label: Eat Safe: Hygiene standards and vendor training
Eat Healthy: Reduce salt, sugar, trans fats
Eat Sustainably: Local seasonal foods, eliminate waste

steps.title: Clean street food hubs and vendor certification
steps.tx: Recognizing that millions of citizens consume food prepared by informal street food vendors daily, FSSAI implements the **clean street food hub certification**. Municipal authorities audit popular street food clusters against strict sanitary criteria, ensuring potable running water, pest-proof waste bins, personal protective aprons and caps for vendors, food safety training, and periodic bacteriological testing of prepared dishes and drinking water.
steps.say: Clean street food hubs guarantee that outdoor food stalls use clean drinking water, wear caps and aprons, and dispose of garbage properly, keeping street dining safe from contamination.

nodes.label: Food handler hygiene training and medical check
Provision of potable water and waste disposal
Formal FSSAI Clean Street Food Hub certification
